QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_45

question.text: What is the settlement mechanism for options on bond futures?

answer.text: Premium settlement on T+1 (buyer pays premium to seller) and exercise settlement upon expiry
Premium and exercise settlement both happen at expiry
Premium is settled real-time and exercise on T+3
Options are converted to futures positions and settled via daily MTM

explanation.text: The Logic: Option premium settlement occurs on T+1 (the day after the trade). The buyer pays the premium to the seller. Upon exercise at expiry, the exercise settlement occurs based on the difference between strike and FSP. The Trap: Premium is not deferred to expiry - it is settled upfront on T+1. Exercise settlement is T+1 from expiry, not T+3. While exercise may convert to futures, the settlement mechanism is distinct. Cross-Exam Context: Option settlement structure is similar across equity (Series VIII) and IRD (Series IV): upfront premium + exercise at expiry. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Option sellers must maintain margins throughout the contract life since they have ongoing obligations. Buyers pay premium upfront and their maximum risk is limited to that premium.
